_topic: Projects — portfolio tiles and image carousels
_help: Add or delete whole project objects freely. Each id maps to public/projects/<id>/; list every screenshot in display order using zero-padded filenames.

_field_help.id: Stable URL-safe identifier. It must exactly match the project's folder under public/projects.
_field_help.name: Short. 'Wavelength', not 'Wavelength — A Realtime Audio Tool'.
_field_help.tagline: One line under ~50 chars. Shows on the tile.
_field_help.description: 2-4 sentences: the problem it solves, what you built, what was interesting. Scale, users, tricky bugs, and perf wins all read well.
_field_help.link: Live demo URL. Leave "" if there isn't one — the button just won't render.
_field_help.images: Ordered public paths. The first image is the tile thumbnail; multiple images appear in the detail carousel.

items.name: Praxis
items.tagline: Develop your SaaS in days not months
items.description: Praxis CLI is a scaffolding tool that speeds up project setup with pre-configured, best-practice templates and automated workflows. It supports flexible frontend choices and a fully independent, production-ready backend with built-in features like authentication, caching, and monitoring. Designed for scalability and modularity, it enables efficient full-stack development without tight coupling between frontend and backend to elevate developer's experience and productivity.

items.name: Praxis Pro
items.tagline: Elevate your SaaS backend with Django
items.description: Praxis Pro is an advanced backend-focused evolution of PRAXIS, built on Django to provide a production-grade foundation with powerful built-in features like ORM, authentication, and admin tools. It automates setup, integrates modern tooling (ELK, Kubernetes, Sentry), and delivers a scalable, best-practice backend architecture. Designed as a workflow accelerator, it helps developers build complex backend systems more efficiently.

items.name: GitBundle
items.tagline: Enhance your GitHub workflow with three independent tools
items.description: GitBundle combines three independent tools to enhance your GitHub workflow: a smart CLI for automated commits (no AI, save your tokens), an AI-powered repo analysis app, and a visual 'year in review' generator. You can use each tool separately or together to streamline development, gain insights, and showcase activity.

items.name: Dev-Tools
items.tagline: A collection of useful development tools
items.description: A developer toolkit featuring an AI-powered README generator, Prisma-to-Express API scaffolder, and SEO meta. It automates documentation, scans codebases intelligently, and generates full CRUD APIs with validation and structure. Built for speed and clarity, it streamlines setup while producing production-ready outputs.

items.name: DevXp
items.tagline: A technical blog to level up your developer experience
items.description: DevXp is a technical blog platform focused on improving developer experience through in-depth articles and practical guides. Built with a modern TypeScript stack, it delivers fast page loads, clean typography, and a distraction-free reading experience.

items.name: Vibe Coding Bundle
items.tagline: Prompt engineering tools for better LLM results
items.description: A collection of AI prompt engineering tools that lint, optimize, and compress prompts for better LLM interactions. It helps developers cut token waste, catch ambiguous phrasing, and ship consistent prompts across projects.

items.name: Mock-Me
items.description: Mock-Me spins up FastAPI mock servers instantly with zero code, letting frontend teams develop against realistic APIs before the backend exists. Define endpoints and payloads declaratively and get a running server with validation out of the box.

items.name: OptiMac
items.description: OptiMac is a maintenance tool for macOS that automates cleanup, monitors system health, and keeps your machine running fast. It bundles common upkeep tasks — cache purging, storage analysis, and process checks — into one simple interface.

items.name: media automations
items.tagline: A macOS CLI for oversized, wrong-format files
items.description: media automations is an interactive macOS CLI, published on npm and launched with a single auto command, that converts images, documents and data, strips backgrounds, and compresses video — 24 image formats including HEIC and camera RAW, 21 video containers, and nothing ever leaves the machine. The expensive work is done by macOS's own frameworks rather than heavy dependencies: two small Swift helpers call Vision for subject masking and WebKit for PDF rendering, so there is no 170 MB background-removal model and no bundled Chromium, and because they ship as source and compile on first use the 56 KB package stays architecture-independent. Compression runs at three levels — on a mixed folder of a 4 MB phone photo, a UI screenshot and a 5-second 4K clip, normal saves 60%, super 86% and ultra 95%. Needs macOS 14 or newer and the Xcode Command Line Tools.
